## Unblinding

Compound: **methotrexate** (PubChem CID [126941](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/126941))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: Dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor

## Verdict (computed by code)

Correct: agent said **DNA replication**, BBBC021 annotates **DNA replication**.

## Reflection

The DNA replication call was driven by the extreme, consistent nuc_dna_mean loss (z -9.8 to -12.9) paired with enlarged cells (cell_area z +5.6 to +8.9) from 10 uM down to 0.003 uM in e2, e3 and e7-e10, plus the atlas plurality for DNA replication (4/10) in e5. Low frac_mitotic_like in e15 and lack of cytoskeletal disruption in e4 correctly down-weighted Eg5, Aurora and microtubule stabilizer/destabilizer classes.

The flat dose_responses in e11 (rho +0.20) and e14 (rho +0.03) were read as saturation, but the acquisition choice to consume all six wells within 0.003-10 uM left potency undefined because even the lowest dose was already maximal. I also over-retained Kinase inhibitors at 0.12 based on 3/10 noisy atlas neighbours in e5 and DNA damage at 0.15 without a discriminating gammaH2AX or cell-cycle measurement.

Unblinding to methotrexate, a dihydrofolate reductase inhibitor, fits an antimetabolite S-phase block under the DNA replication class rather than direct replisome inhibition, consistent with S-phase disruption causing instability (PMID 7606822).

What was right:
- Flagged potent replication block from nuc_dna_mean z -10 to -13 with cell_area z +5 to +9 across all 6 doses in e2, e3, e7-e10
- Used atlas comparison in e5 (DNA replication 4/10) to prioritize DNA replication over cytoskeletal classes
- Ruled out Aurora, Eg5 and microtubule classes via enlarged non-mitotic morphology and flat/decreased frac_mitotic_like in e15

What was wrong or missed:
- Sampled only within the saturated 0.003-10 uM range, so dose_response tests in e11-e14 were flat and potency/onset was never defined
- Retained Kinase inhibitors at 0.12 from 3/10 atlas neighbours in e5 despite no supporting morphology
- Retained DNA damage at 0.15 without acquiring a discriminating DNA-damage readout to separate S-phase depletion from direct damage

Proposed next experiment: EdU pulse with DNA-content flow cytometry plus gammaH2AX staining with and without leucovorin/thymidine-hypoxanthine rescue and washout to confirm S-phase block versus DNA damage and DHFR-dependent antimetabolite mechanism.
